bss.topic: Formas de relevo: montanhas, planaltos, planícies e depressões

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é relevo?
options: o conjunto das formas da superfície da Terra
a quantidade de chuva de um lugar
o tipo de vegetação de uma região
questions.answer: o conjunto das formas da superfície da Terra
questions.hint: Pense nas partes altas e baixas do terreno.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual forma de relevo é muito alta e tem encostas íngremes?
questions.hint: Escalar essa forma de relevo dá bastante trabalho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como é uma planície?
options: um terreno plano e baixo, geralmente perto de rios ou do mar
um terreno muito alto e pontudo
um buraco no meio de montanhas
questions.answer: um terreno plano e baixo, geralmente perto de rios ou do mar
questions.hint: Pense em um lugar onde os rios deixam areia e barro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como é um planalto?
options: um terreno elevado e com a parte de cima mais ou menos plana
um terreno abaixo do nível do mar
questions.answer: um terreno elevado e com a parte de cima mais ou menos plana
questions.hint: O nome junta 'plano' e 'alto'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é uma depressão no relevo?
options: uma área mais baixa que os terrenos ao seu redor
a montanha mais alta de um país
uma ilha no meio do mar
questions.answer: uma área mais baixa que os terrenos ao seu redor
questions.hint: Pense em algo afundado em relação ao que está em volta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A cidade de São Paulo fica em qual forma de relevo?
questions.hint: É um terreno alto e quase plano, bem acima do nível do mar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual serra separa a cidade de São Paulo do litoral paulista?
questions.hint: Quem desce de São Paulo para a praia passa por ela.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Ao descer de São Paulo até Santos, o terreno vai...
options: do planalto até a planície do litoral
de uma montanha até outra montanha
questions.answer: do planalto até a planície do litoral
questions.hint: Santos fica à beira-mar, bem mais baixo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o ponto mais alto do Brasil?
questions.hint: Fica no norte do Brasil, quase sempre coberto por nuvens.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O Pantanal é uma grande área plana e baixa que alaga na época das chuvas. Que forma de relevo ele é?
questions.hint: Terreno plano e baixo, onde a água se espalha.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes lugares fica em uma planície?
questions.hint: Procure o lugar mais baixo e plano.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em qual forma de relevo os rios costumam depositar areia e barro?
questions.hint: A água corre devagar em terrenos baixos e planos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que muitas cidades foram construídas em planícies e planaltos?
options: porque é mais fácil construir casas e estradas em terrenos planos
porque não existem rios nesses lugares
questions.answer: porque é mais fácil construir casas e estradas em terrenos planos
questions.hint: Pense em como seria construir uma rua numa encosta íngreme.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual frase compara corretamente o planalto e a planície?
options: os dois são planos, mas o planalto é mais alto
a planície é sempre mais alta que o planalto
questions.answer: os dois são planos, mas o planalto é mais alto
questions.hint: Lembre o que cada nome quer dizer.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Imagine que você vai de carro de São Paulo até a praia. Descreva como o relevo muda pelo caminho.
questions.hint: Use as palavras planalto, serra e planície.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o relevo pode atrapalhar ou ajudar a construção de uma estrada? Dê um exemplo.
questions.hint: Pense em subidas, curvas e terrenos planos.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main purpose of a procedural text?
options: to tell the reader how to do or make something
questions.answer: to tell the reader how to do or make something
questions.hint: Think of a recipe or a set of game rules.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a procedural text?
options: a fairy tale about a dragon
questions.hint: Which one has steps to follow?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is written as an instruction (using an imperative verb)?
options: Pour the water into the jug.
The water was in the jug.
questions.answer: Pour the water into the jug.
questions.hint: Instructions usually start with a bossy verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which section usually comes first in a set of instructions?
options: a list of what you will need
a warning at the very end
questions.answer: a list of what you will need
questions.hint: You need to get everything ready before you start.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which adverb makes this instruction more precise? 'Stir the mixture ___ so it doesn't spill.'
questions.hint: Think about how you stir something without splashing it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Find the adverb in this instruction: 'Carefully cut the paper along the dotted line.'
questions.hint: It tells you how to cut.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which instruction is the most precise?
options: Bake the cake for 25 minutes at 180°C.
Bake the cake for a while.
Put the cake in somewhere hot.
questions.answer: Bake the cake for 25 minutes at 180°C.
questions.hint: Look for exact numbers.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is a time connective that helps put steps in order?
questions.hint: It tells you when to do something.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a warning for the reader?
options: Be careful: the pan will be very hot!
questions.answer: Be careful: the pan will be very hot!
questions.hint: A warning helps keep the reader safe.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is a helpful tip?
options: Tip: wet your hands so the dough doesn't stick.
questions.answer: Tip: wet your hands so the dough doesn't stick.
questions.hint: A tip gives extra advice to make the task easier.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which adverb best completes this instruction? 'Hold the glass ___ with both hands.'
questions.hint: You don't want to drop it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why are numbered steps useful in instructions?
options: they show the reader the order to do things
they tell the reader a story
questions.answer: they show the reader the order to do things
questions.hint: Think about what would happen if you did the steps in the wrong order.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which instruction is clearer for a reader?
options: Fold the paper in half from top to bottom.
questions.answer: Fold the paper in half from top to bottom.
questions.hint: A clear instruction says exactly what and how.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best title for a procedural text?
options: How to Plant a Sunflower Seed
questions.answer: How to Plant a Sunflower Seed
questions.hint: Procedural titles often start with 'How to'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite this instruction to make it more precise, adding an adverb and an exact amount: 'Add some water to the paint.'
questions.hint: Say how much water and how to add it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one tip or one warning for someone learning to ride a bike.
questions.hint: Think about what could go wrong or what makes it easier.

en_read.topic: Relationships in adventure fiction — 'Kensuke's Kingdom' (Michael Morpurgo)

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A "relationship" in a story is…
options: the way two characters feel about and treat each other
the place where the story happens
the last chapter of a book
questions.answer: the way two characters feel about and treat each other
questions.hint: Think about two characters together.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: When you "infer", you…
options: work out something the author has not said directly
copy a sentence from the text
questions.answer: work out something the author has not said directly
questions.hint: It is like being a detective.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "Mia stamped past the old fisherman without saying hello." What can you infer about how Mia feels towards him?
options: she is unfriendly or cross with him
she is scared of the sea
questions.answer: she is unfriendly or cross with him
questions.hint: What does stamping and not saying hello show?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "Every evening, the old keeper left a bowl of soup outside Ravi's tent, but he never stayed to talk." What does this suggest about the keeper?
options: he cares about Ravi but is shy or distant
he does not know Ravi is there
questions.answer: he cares about Ravi but is shy or distant
questions.hint: Think about the soup and the silence together.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which detail would be the best evidence that two characters have become friends?
options: One of them has a red hat.
questions.hint: Evidence must link to the relationship.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In Chapter 1 a girl refuses to share her food with a stranger. In Chapter 8 she cooks him dinner. This shows that their relationship has…
questions.hint: Compare the beginning with later.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Using evidence from several chapters helps you see how a relationship ___ over time. Write one word meaning "becomes different".
questions.hint: It is one of this week's keywords.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "At first, Leo hid whenever the castaway came near. By the end of the summer, he waited on the beach for him every morning." Which word best describes the change in Leo?
questions.hint: Look at "At first" and "By the end".

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which phrase from a story is a time clue showing that a relationship has changed?
questions.hint: Look for a phrase about time passing.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "The old man said nothing, but he moved over to make space for Kit on the rock." What can you infer?
options: he is starting to accept Kit
he wants Kit to fall in
he is too tired to talk
questions.answer: he is starting to accept Kit
questions.hint: Actions can speak louder than words.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In adventure stories, characters who are stranded together often become closer because…
options: they must rely on each other to survive
they live in the same street
they go to the same school
questions.answer: they must rely on each other to survive
questions.hint: Think about danger and teamwork.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "Zara snatched the map and marched off alone." Later: "Zara handed Ben the map. 'You lead,' she said." What is the best inference?
questions.hint: Compare what she does with the map each time.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is the strongest way to begin an answer about how a relationship changes?
options: "At the start, the characters distrust each other, but later…"
questions.answer: "At the start, the characters distrust each other, but later…"
questions.hint: A good answer compares the beginning with later.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "When the storm came, Sam held the rope tightly so that Grandpa Ott would not be swept away. Grandpa Ott had once called Sam 'a useless boy'." How has the relationship changed? Use evidence from both sentences.
questions.hint: Compare what Grandpa Ott once said with what Sam does now.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: "On the first day, the stranger shouted at Nell to leave his island. On the last day, he gave her his carved wooden turtle and turned away so she would not see his tears." What can you infer about his feelings for Nell at the end? Explain your evidence.
questions.hint: Think about the gift and the tears.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Think of two characters in a story you have read whose relationship changed. Explain how it changed, giving one piece of evidence from the beginning and one from later on.
questions.hint: Use "At first…" and "Later…".

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word is spelt correctly?
questions.hint: This person acts in plays and films.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: sail _ _ (a person who works on a ship)
questions.hint: This job ends in -or, not -er.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means "a person who visits"?
questions.hint: Think of the -or suffix.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: doct _ _
questions.hint: You see this person when you are ill.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add the suffix to the verb "direct" to make a word for the person who directs a film.
questions.hint: It ends in -or.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means "a person who edits a newspaper or book"?
questions.hint: Add -or to "edit".

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: conduct _ _ (a person who leads an orchestra)
questions.hint: conduct + a two-letter suffix

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means "a person who survives a disaster"?
questions.hint: Drop the e from "survive" before the suffix.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: instruct _ _ (a person who teaches a skill, such as swimming)
questions.hint: instruct + a two-letter suffix

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word ends with -er, NOT -or?
questions.hint: Most job words use -er; only some use -or.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which pair is spelt correctly?
questions.hint: One uses -or and one uses -er.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: "Survive" becomes "survivor". What happens to the final e?
questions.hint: Look at the letters after "surviv".

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Complete the sentence: The ___ shouted "Action!" and the cameras began to roll.
questions.hint: This person is in charge of making a film.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: directer → director; acter → actor; sailer → sailor; survivar → survivor; editer → editor
questions.hint: All five wrong words are jobs or people that should end in -or.
questions.text: The film directer asked a famous acter to play a brave sailer. In the story, an old doctor helps a lonely survivar escape from an island. A newspaper editer said it was the best film of the year.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling of the word for a person who invents things is correct?
questions.hint: It uses the less common people suffix.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words, then check every job word ends correctly.
questions.answer: instructer → instructor; inventer → inventor; visiter → visitor; docter → doctor; conducter → conductor
questions.hint: Look for people words with the wrong ending.
questions.text: Our swimming instructer is also an inventer. He made a machine that helps every visiter float. Last week a docter and a train conducter came to watch our lesson at the pool. They both clapped loudly when my little brother finally swam all the way across without any help.

ipc.topic: Explorers and Adventurers: Zheng He and Columbus — voyages across oceans

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: A long journey by sea is called a…
questions.hint: It is one of this week's keywords.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which country did Zheng He come from?
questions.hint: He sailed for the Ming emperor.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: In which year did Columbus first cross the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.hint: It was at the end of the 1400s.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which ocean did Columbus cross on his first voyage?
questions.hint: It lies between Europe and the Americas.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which ocean did Zheng He's fleets cross to reach India, Arabia and East Africa?
questions.hint: This ocean is named after a country on its shore.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which country's king and queen paid for Columbus's first voyage?
questions.hint: He set sail from this country in 1492.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: How many ships did Columbus take on his first voyage?
questions.hint: Think of the Niña, the Pinta and the Santa María.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Zheng He led a series of great voyages. How many voyages did he lead?
questions.hint: It is the same as the number of days in a week.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which place did Columbus reach in 1492?
questions.hint: He landed on islands west of the Atlantic.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Where did Columbus believe he had arrived?
questions.hint: This is why he called the people he met "Indians".

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: How did Zheng He's fleet compare with Columbus's fleet?
questions.hint: Zheng He sailed with very large "treasure ships".

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which voyages happened first?
options: they happened at the same time
questions.hint: Zheng He sailed in the early 1400s.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What is the word for the path that a ship follows from one place to another?
questions.hint: You can trace it on a map with a line.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which tool helped both explorers find their direction at sea?
questions.hint: Its needle points north.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Give one similarity and one difference between the voyages of Zheng He and Columbus.
questions.hint: Think about the size of the fleets, the oceans and what they were looking for.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Columbus's voyages changed life for the people already living in the Americas. Why is it important to think about their point of view too?
questions.hint: Think about who was there before the ships arrived.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A café has 3 kinds of bread and 4 kinds of filling. How many different sandwiches with one bread and one filling can be made?
questions.hint: Each bread can go with every filling.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A tree is 4 m tall. A tower is 3 times as tall. How tall is the tower in metres?
questions.hint: "3 times as tall" means multiply.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Each bike has 2 wheels. How many wheels are on 9 bikes?
questions.hint: One bike goes with 2 wheels.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Lily has 5 T-shirts and 3 pairs of shorts. How many different outfits of one T-shirt and one pair of shorts can she make?
questions.hint: Multiply the choices.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A pencil is 15 cm long. A ruler is 2 times as long. How long is the ruler in centimetres?
questions.hint: Double 15.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: There are 6 tables and each table has 4 chairs. How many chairs are there?
questions.hint: 1 table → 4 chairs.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A dog eats 3 tins of food a week. How many tins does it eat in 8 weeks?
questions.hint: Each week goes with 3 tins.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A tower is 36 m tall. It is 4 times as tall as a house. How tall is the house in metres?
questions.hint: Work backwards: divide.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: An ice-cream shop has 6 flavours and 2 kinds of cone. How many different single-scoop ice creams can be made?
questions.hint: Each flavour can go in each cone.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A recipe uses 2 eggs for every 1 cake. How many eggs are needed for 7 cakes?
questions.hint: 1 cake → 2 eggs.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Sam has 8 stickers. Ana has 5 times as many. How many stickers does Ana have?
questions.hint: Multiply by 5.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A menu has 4 starters, 3 main courses and 2 desserts. How many different 3-course meals can be made?
questions.hint: Multiply all three numbers.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A school has 7 classes. Each class needs 6 paintbrushes. Each paintbrush costs £2. How much do all the paintbrushes cost in pounds?
questions.hint: First find how many brushes, then the cost.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A bag of apples weighs 3 kg. A sack of potatoes is 6 times as heavy. What is the difference in weight between them, in kilograms?
questions.hint: Find the sack's weight first, then subtract.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Tom can make 20 outfits from some T-shirts and 4 pairs of trousers. How many T-shirts does he have?
questions.hint: What times 4 makes 20?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain the difference between "3 more than 6" and "3 times as many as 6". Give the answer to each.
questions.hint: One means adding, the other means multiplying.
